newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY - MULLER GIVES LEAFS OVERTIME WIN OVER CHICAGO.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY - MULLER GIVES LEAFS OVERTIME WIN OVER CHICAGO.

text.p: Kirk Muller scored from a near-impossible angle 2:07 into overtime, giving the Toronto Maple Leafs a 2-1 victory over the Chicago Blackhawks Friday and snapping their five-game road losing streak.
Chicago played amid rampant speculation that star goaltender Ed Belfour would be traded. He was not in the lineup for the game.
Toronto's Todd Warriner worked the puck out of the left corner and lifted a backhander that hit goaltender Jeff Hackett in the chest.
The puck caromed to Muller, who cut down from the faceoff circle to the goal line and put a shot under the crossbar for his 15th goal of the season and fifth against Chicago.
"Just enough of an opening, I guess, to sneak it in. Hackett didn't leave me much," Muller said. "This was a huge win for us."
Larry Murphy also scored for the Maple Leafs, who have posted back-to-back wins following a seven-game losing streak.
Tony Amonte had the only goal for the Blackhawks, who debuted their new "third" jerseys, but fell to 1-5-1 in their last seven home games.
Felix Potvin made 27 saves for Toronto, while Hackett turned aside 31 in place of Belfour.
"There's a deal pending with another club regarding Ed Belfour and the other team asked us not to play him tonight," said Jim DeMaria, the Blackhawks director of media relations.

"We just tried to put the Eddie thing aside and I think we did and it really had no effect for us," Amonte said. "It's tough to see a friend go, but the rest of us our still here. We're still Blackhawks and we have to get going."

In Hartford, Derek King recorded a natural hat trick, his first in more than three years, Zigmund Palffy tallied twice and Rick Bowness won in his first game as head coach as the New York Islanders beat the Whalers 5-2.
Bowness was promoted from associate coach before the game after general manager Mike Milbury relinquished his duties as head coach.
"Every hockey team has to skate, work and be tough to play against. Tonight, we were difficult to play against," said Bowness, who coached previously with Winnipeg, Boston and Ottawa.
Geoff Sanderson and Steven Rice had the goals for the Whalers, who were trying for their third straight win.

In Buffalo, Daniel McGillis set up Ryan Smyth's game-winning goal in the third period and added an insurance tally after a disallowed goal as the Edmonton Oilers ended the Sabres' eight-game home unbeaten streak with a 3-1 victory.

Smyth took a pass from McGillis and broke up the right wing before snapping a wrist shot past goaltender Steve Shields from the right faceoff circle for his 24th goal and a 2-1 edge with 8:31 remaining.
An apparent tying goal by Buffalo's Donald Audette was disallowed 42 seconds later when teammate Brad May was penalised for interfering with goalie Curtis Joseph.
Andrei Kovalenko had the other Edmonton tally while Rob Ray scored the lone goal for Buffalo, which had its four-game winning streak stopped.

In Ottawa, Daniel Alfredsson tipped a shot past Trevor Kidd with 30 seconds left in regulation, lifting the Senators into a 2-2 tie with the Calgary Flames in a battle of the lowest-scoring teams in the NHL.
Alexei Yashin also scored for Ottawa, which has only one win in its last seven home games.
Corey Millen tallied twice for the Flames, who are 1-3-1 in their last five games.
In San Jose, Martin Brodeur made 18 saves and Steve Sullivan's goal broke a tie late in the second period as the New Jersey Devils held on for a 3-1 victory over the Sharks.
Valeri Zelepukin and John MacLean also tallied and Dave Andreychuk picked up a pair of assists for the Devils, who have won three of its last four games and completed a 2-1 West Coast road trip.
Steve Guolla scored for San Jose.
At Washington, Darryl Sydor and Mike Modano scored on the power play in a three-goal second period and Arturs Irbe made 36 saves as the Dallas Stars defeated the Capitals 5-2.

Sydor, Modano and Dave Reid each had a goal and an assist while Pat Verbeek and Brent Gilchrist contributed two assists apiece for the Stars, who improved to 8-2-2 on the road against Eastern Conference opponents. Dallas leads the league with 15 road wins.
